summary: Lower `extends` to C# inheritance only when the base constructor is statically resolved to a compatible translated class and prototype dynamics are excluded.

target.notes: Emit `$D : $B` and apply constructor, field-order, method-override, static-member, and super rules independently.

semantics.instance_prototype_chain: represented by C# type inheritance only under closed-world requirements

caveats: JavaScript `extends` establishes both instance-prototype and constructor-object prototype relationships; C# inheritance covers only the closed-world instance/type portion.

tests.name: simple inheritance
tests.input: class B { m(){return 1;} } class D extends B {} console.log(new D().m());

tests.name: edge: dynamic base excluded
tests.input: function chooseBase(){ console.log('choose'); return class { m(){ return 1; } }; } const Base = chooseBase(); class D extends Base {} new D();
tests.expected_behavior: prints choose while evaluating Base; the chosen constructor is a runtime value and this rule must not match without stronger analysis
